physics_gate_2.doppler_convention: physics/relativity.gd doppler_apparent = 1/(gamma (1 - beta cos theta')) with theta' the apparent angle; the sky shader (sky/background.gdshader:40-47) forms d = 1/(g (1 + b c)) with c = n'.(-beta_hat), the same thing, with 1 + b c rewritten through one_minus_beta (float64 on the CPU) when c < 0. Oracle: at 0.99c D(90') = 0.14107 = 1/gamma, D(acos 0.99 = 8.1096 deg) = 7.0888 = gamma, D = 1 at theta' = 29.8181 deg. Sideways is darker.

physics_gate_2.renders_verdict: Opened exposure_sheet.png, contact_sheet.png and the eight single frames at rest and 0.99c. Rest eye (EV -4.4): a credible dark-site naked-eye sky, stars to ~V 6 and a faint Milky Way; rest camera (EV -8.3): a long-exposure photograph of the same view. 0.99c starboard eye and camera-fixed: nearly black with the blueshift glow entering from the forward edge, sideways darkening shown at a fixed exposure as physics. 0.99c camera-auto at the EV -20 clamp: blown out with redshifted orange stars, labelled, the meter hiding the physics as intended. 0.99c forward eye: the compressed blue-white disk has a radius of about 220 px at 70 deg vertical FOV, which is the D = 1 boundary at 29.8 deg (270 x tan 29.8 / tan 35 = 221 px). Contact sheet across 0.5/0.9/0.99c is monotone and consistent. Gate 2 passes for what the milestone claims; the absolute Milky Way level is the open calibration question (deviation 1).

findings.title: The panorama's absolute Milky Way level rests on an uncited 20 mag/arcsec^2 anchored to a photo quantile
findings.detail: see deviations[0]; this is the one physics item gate 2 cannot sign off, and it is already flagged for R-d. Not blocking the milestone: the dark patch (22) is calibrated through the package and tested, and the exponent is a single constant that recalibrates automatically when the anchor changes.

findings.title: EV_dark follows Omega_px because the PSF is fixed in pixels, so the extended sky's displayed brightness depends on the render size
findings.detail: L(22) renders at linear 3.0e-3 at 960x540 and 4.2e-4 at 2560x1440 (factor 7.1). V_lim is held constant by construction, the sky is not. A PSF fixed in angle (sigma in arcmin, clamped to >= ~0.7 px for antialiasing) would make the star peak a physical quantity and EV_dark a constant; recommend for M1.5b or a follow-up, with the ladder re-run at both sizes.

findings.title: The meter sees only the panorama, never the stars, and is a plain log-average over the whole 102 x 70 deg view
findings.detail: At 0.99c forward it reads 6.0e-5 cd/m^2, below the rest-frame 4.4e-4, because the redshifted periphery dominates the log mean while the D = 14 centre is a headlight; so eye mode never light-adapts forward. Acceptable for M1.5a (eye adaptation is out of scope) but the forward CMB (M1.8) will need the meter to include stars and to weight the centre, or the 'eye light-adapts' sentence in the docs will be untrue in the one case that matters.

deviations.what: Panorama un-stretch: power law on luminance anchored at 22 (dark caps median) and 20 mag/arcsec^2 (99.9th-percentile luminance of the photo), exponent 0.32
deviations.verdict: ACCEPT for M1.5a as an explicitly flagged assumption; the anchor must be replaced by a cited value before M1.5b lands. The un-stretch itself is the right kind of fix (a linear calibration put the Milky Way ~6 mag too bright) but it is not physically honest in the strict sense: it assumes the NOIRLab image is a pure luminance gamma, when a processed photograph has curves, local contrast and per-channel work, and the chromaticity-preserving form bakes the photo's colour processing in. On 20 mag/arcsec^2: I know of no measurement that puts degree-scale integrated Milky Way light at 20.0 in V. Leinert et al. 1998 (A&AS 127, 1, Table 16, Pioneer 10 integrated starlight of stars fainter than 6.5 mag, Toller 1981) give galactic-plane maxima of a few hundred S10(V) toward Sagittarius/Scutum/Carina, i.e. roughly 20.8-21.3 mag/arcsec^2 (300 S10 = 21.6, 600 S10 = 20.8), and the SQM-scale natural-sky model of Duriscoe 2013 (PASP 125, 1370) puts the brightest Sagittarius region near 20.5-21 including the airglow/zodiacal pedestal. Only the bulge at arcminute resolution (Baade's Window, Terndrup 1988, V ~ 18.3) is brighter, and a 10k-pixel equal-area 99.9th percentile (about 40 deg^2) does not resolve that. So 20 is at the bright end by roughly 0.5-1 mag; 20.5-21 is defensible with a citation, 20 is not. Note the destarred panorama should represent light the drawn tiers do NOT carry (the drawn stars already sum to 2.7e-4 lx, 24.3 mag/arcsec^2 spread over the sphere), so the ISL-fainter-than-6.5 table is the right class of reference. Most defensible alternative: fit the exponent (or a per-bin scale) to several cited bins rather than to one quantile, e.g. Leinert Table 16 values at the galactic poles and at three plane longitudes compared with the panorama's equal-area mip at the same positions, and report the residuals; or, cleaner and fully consistent with the game's own catalogue, build a Gaia/Tycho-2 integrated-flux map per HEALPix bin of the stars below the drawn cut (G -> V through the package) and use the photo only as sub-bin texture (photo divided by its own bin mean). That makes the background's cd/m^2 a measured quantity and removes the double counting between the starfield and the panorama.

deviations.what: No pinhole cos^3 correction on stars (sky/starfield.gdshader:19-24)
deviations.verdict: ACCEPT. For a viewer at the centre of projection the cos^3 term is real (an edge pixel subtends less solid angle, so the same E_v needs a larger pixel sum), but players view a 102 x 70 deg frustum as a picture from far outside its centre of projection, where uniform pixel sums are what keeps V-ordering legible; the executor measured 2.6x at the edge and chose ordering. Documented in the shader. No test depends on it (goldens and ladder are at the centre, cos^3 < 0.5%). Revisit only if head-tracked/VR output arrives.

deviations.what: EV_dark depends on render size through Omega_px (sky/exposure.gd:84)
deviations.verdict: ACCEPT WITH FINDING (P2 above). The derivation is correct for a PSF fixed in pixels, and it is what keeps AC8 resolution-independent (-4.39 at 540 rows, -1.56 at 1440), but the consequence that the extended sky's displayed brightness scales with 1/Omega_px (x7.1 between the two sizes) is the wrong invariant: the eye's threshold is set by the sky's luminance, which should look the same at any resolution. An angular PSF fixes both at once.

deviations.what: Camera auto at 0.99c starboard hits the -20 EV clamp and blows out, deliberately
deviations.verdict: ACCEPT. It is labelled on the HUD and in the sheet, and it is exactly the 'meter hides physics' lesson the corrected F5 asks for. The default clamp is unphysical (a real camera bottoms out near EV100 -14); tightening it would make the same point with a camera limit instead of an arbitrary number.

deviations.what: Eye mode stays at EV_dark forward at 0.99c
deviations.verdict: ACCEPT for M1.5a, with the P3 finding on the meter. The log-average meter over the full view legitimately reads below the rest frame forward (6.0e-5 vs 4.4e-4 cd/m^2) because 70% of the frustum is redshifted; the resulting render (a saturated headlight disk on a dark-adapted eye) is a fair picture of what a dark-adapted observer would see before adapting. A true adaptation model is out of M1.5a's scope but must come with M1.8's CMB glow.
FIX before merge (one-line edit); scored under code quality. The notes field already states the correct physics, so no physics risk.

deviations.what: 22 mag/arcsec^2 is a ground-site value; from space it is about 23
deviations.verdict: KEEP 22 FOR M1.5a, RELABEL, AND OPEN A LEDGER ROW. 22.0 (V, zenith, dark site) includes airglow (~50-100 S10) and zodiacal light (~60-100 S10) that an interstellar ship never sees. Near Earth outside the atmosphere the zodiacal light alone keeps the ecliptic-pole sky near 23.0-23.3; outside the zodiacal cloud the galactic caps are integrated starlight (~25-30 S10 fainter than 6.5 mag = ~24.1) plus diffuse galactic light and the EBL, i.e. about 23.5-24 in V. With the Crumey model that moves V_lim(F = 2) from 6.26 (22) to 6.68 (23), 6.90 (23.5) and 7.12 (24), and the AC8 window 6.0-6.8 was written against the ground value, so the change is a design decision (the AC8 window moves with it) rather than a code fix. The constant is one number (Exposure.DARK_SKY_MAG) and everything recalibrates from it, including the un-stretch exponent, which is why the Milky Way anchor (deviation 1) must be settled at the same time: with 23.5/21 the exponent is 0.41, with 22/20 it is 0.32.
